question: Should OpenClaw adopt an inspect-only skill capability-manifest v0 first, or sponsor a broader permission contract that includes consent and enforceable runtime semantics?
rationale: The choice defines a public skill metadata and security contract across ClawHub, installation, hooks, and future enforcement; source-level implementation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow inspect-only v0
options.body: Use the capability declaration and inspection direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74594, preserving existing runtime behavior while establishing a versioned vocabulary.

options.title: Design the full permission contract first
options.body: Define consent, update diffs, declaration accuracy, enforcement ownership, signing, and attestation together before accepting a manifest surface.

options.title: Keep the work external for now
options.body: Leave ecosystem experimentation in ClawHub and external tools until OpenClaw has an agreed policy and enforcement model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow inspect-only v0
recommendation.body: Use the capability declaration and inspection direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74594, preserving existing runtime behavior while establishing a versioned vocabulary.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue's recorded product-security direction and repository vision context point to this decision needing explicit ecosystem-level sponsorship.
